title: THE OFFERING FOR THE UNSEEN WRONG

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'They are to bring to the priest as a guilt offering a ram from the flock, one without defect and of the proper value. In this way the priest will make atonement for them for the wrong they have committed unintentionally, and they will be forgiven.'" - Lev 5:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the weight of verse 17 — guilty even without knowing — comes verse 18, and its final word is forgiven.

God never leaves a diagnosis without a remedy. He tells us how deep the problem goes, and in the same breath He tells us it is covered.

This is a pattern worth learning to recognise in Scripture. God is always more honest about our condition than we are, and always more generous with His provision than we expect. He does not soften the diagnosis to make us feel better; He supplies a cure large enough to handle the truth.

Paul does exactly this in Romans. Chapter after chapter of unflinching diagnosis — none is righteous, not even one — and then: But now a righteousness from God, apart from the law, has been made known (Rom 3:21). The bad news is worse than we thought. The good news is better.

If you have ever avoided honest self-examination because you were afraid of what you would find, this verse is for you. You can afford to look. The provision was made before you looked, and it does not depend on what you discover.

Guilty, even unknowingly. And forgiven, completely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I avoid honest self-examination out of fear of what I will find?
2. Can I hold both truths together — that I am worse than I know, and fully forgiven in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know me better than I know myself, and You have provided for all of it. Give me courage to look honestly, resting in Christ. Amen.
